cohorts.summary: Early players encounter immediate game over conditions upon the protagonist's death and punishing high difficulties, alongside structurally repetitive dungeon designs.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the combat system immediately triggers a game over if the main character dies, regardless of whether other party members could revive them.

citations.review_text: I love the music in the game the main cast are all really charming and a friend group that acts like an actual friend group. The dungeons are a little bit weird because auto generative but I love the combat in the game. Easily the best part of the game is the social simulator.

It starts strong both with high quality anime sequences, excellent soundtrack and frequent voice acting sections.
However, after a  few hours the game lets you go, or rather shoves you into the actual gameplay and it's tiring.

The combat is atrocious. It's super simple with most abilities just doing different types of damage or boosting atk/def. Yet, it's so easy to die which forces you restart the floor. It's one of the games that gives you a game over screen as soon as your main character dies, even if you have revival. The dungeons are super boring only having fights and occasional chests with small rewards. The other gamified aspects, like improving Social Links through spending time with characters are just stat increases with extra steps.

If the game's strong voice acting and music become tiring after the hundred time you've heard it. It's a shame really because the story did seem interesting, but no chance is it worth the excruciating dungeon experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that achieving the true ending and unlocking the Golden content in February requires maxing out Marie's social link and can be very easy to miss without a guide.

citations.review_text:
This is my 4th playthrough. I have already played the game 3x before when it was on the gamepass and now on i am playing it on laptop. The graphics and characters might at first look bad and goofy but trust me, it will grow on you. Personally when you compare the friendship in this game to P5R, it does not feel that forced and it makes you feel like you ARE a part of the friendgroup. 
The only thing that I feel like needs improving is Marie´s social link. It is VERY EASY to miss the Golden content in February if you do not max her social link and even if (I am currently trying my best not to spoil the stuff that happens in Febraury) the player manages to do the content in that month, there is a very high chance that they will miss out on the person that is behind the Midnight Channel. I was kinda mad when I found out what happens when the player decides to visit the Food Court at Junes for the 2nd time after Yu said his Farewells because after the goodbyes the game asks the player if they really want to return back to Dojima´s resident. The way i found out about it was through Youtube AFTER finishing the game and I had 2 choices: The first one was load the last save and unlock the new content and the second one was replay the whole game. I went with the 2nd choice because i also realized that I did not max some characters or did not know about the ones that had one (like the old lady in black where you can find her at the riverbank). Another thing that was a bit annoying is the camera movement in the Dungeons. It feels like rotating a stone and those Golden Hands were a pain in the ass in the beginning of the game since they kept escaping.

Despite missing the Golden Content during my 1st playthrough, I did not experience any major issues at all. The game is pretty good and i find the music is better than P5R (maybe because I am not a fan of Jazz music xD).

i loved it . tho its kinda hard to get the true ending without looking it up , still great story and prob the best characters in all the series , good ending too 
8/10 
oh yeah no more larping cuz i played all games now (we dont talk about 1 and 2)

citations.review_text:
Fantastic game, didn't enjoy it nearly as much as Persona 3 FES but I still loved it. The cast is strong and full of goofy but genuine moments sprinkled in. The soundtrack is amazing too, yukiko's castle and backside of the tv are my favorites (runner up is signs of love [dojima residence]).

Don't buy or play if you want a 'serious' or mature game, you'll be disappointed and hate it.

My only gripes is December 03 (iykyk) and January and February seeming more filler than anything, even more than the early and long 'tutorial' Persona games are known for. 

Definitely worth on sale, I wouldn't pay full price for this and especially don't buy the new demake, this version holds up even in 2026.

This is the most addictive game I ever played, the gameplay, story, music and characters make a incredible experience. My only problem is the beginning, it feels kinda slow. Other than that play this game as soon as you can.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat as repetitive or tedious at times.

citations.review_text:
The Scooby gang solves a serial killing, defeats god and become the bestest friends. 

Fans of this series know what to expect. Lots of Japanese school hijinks, slightly repetitive combat gets brutal on higher difficulty, a great story, some cringe and you'll feel sad when its all over. 

P4 is less dark, despite the serial killer than p3 and p5 I think. Story was great, I was invested and I wanted to see the ending, instead of being desperate to see the ending if you know what I mean coughUbisoftcoughValhalla. 

There are some scenes that have aged badly though. Its a coming of age story yes but the characters are 15-16. It gets creepy really some of the sexualisation. Hoping the remake irons it out a bit! 

Characters are really likeable though. The social links are quite engaging and different. It's well written for sure. 

Graphics are fine, its a older game but hold up well enough. Cut scenes are aimed though which is pretty cool. 

Combat is better than p3. Less tedius but never too boring. Breaking up the dungeons helps a lot. Definitely a difficulty curve at higher difficulty i dialed it back so I could enjoy it with less stress. Skill issue...yes but doesnt detract from the game I don't think. 

On Steam Deck, this was a great experience too. 

So not for everyone but those those it's for you'll love it.

Recommended if you want something relaxing and a beautiful experience without the somewhat tedious grinding of Persona 3. If you want to have a good time, it's a fantastic game. claims.claim: Reviewers describe the dungeon crawling and gameplay as dated, noting that mechanics and boss fights can feel like tedious or unfair slogs that overstay their welcome.

citations.review_text:
This game is incredibly special. It gave me what is easily one of the deepest connections I’ve ever felt to a video game cast and their individual stories and overall the progression of a game. While the dungeon crawling can feel a bit dated and the game definitely shows its age compared to Persona 5 Royal, the overall experience is still deeply rewarding.

In fact, I think I actually enjoyed it more than P5R (which, to be fair, is the only other Persona game I’ve played). The comedy is fantastic, and the jokes consistently land.

Finishing this one is definitely going to leave a bit of a void, but I know I'll look back on it as one of my absolute favorites. It has even motivated me to dive into the rest of the series, including the Persona 4 spinoffs, which I can't wait to try.

This game is so important to me. I played it when I was young and really enjoyed it, but I didn't realize how much it had affected me until years later when Persona 5 came out. After beating P5, I went back and replayed this game, and since then, it's been one of the most important games to me that's ever been made. It is unbelievable how easy it is to get attached to these characters, get invested in this story, and fall in love with this gameplay. 

I will admit, future Persona games have much more refined gameplay, but this game still holds up incredibly well. It's biggest flaws are some QOL features missing that we'd later get such as Shift/Baton Pass, which isn't that big of a deal, and unfortunately terrible boss design. Boss fights in this game can become slogs with such massive health bars they overstay their welcome.

Still, it's difficult NOT to want to keep going purely for what I believe to be one of the best stories in gaming. It is so well-written. 

Persona as a series, and this game as a result, have some persistent writing flaws, but I'd argue this game suffers the least from them. I love this game and nothing will ever change that. Can't wait for P4R <3

Persona 4 Golden is an amazing game that I highly recommend to any JRPG fan. It's pretty simple mechanic-wise compared to other JRPGs but it has a 10/10 plot to make up for that.
 
The gameplay is split between dungeon crawling and a day by day school life where you choose how to spend the day. What you do in your school life may also end up being helpful in battles. There are a lot of characters you can hang out and bond with so you can learn more about them (this game in my opinion also has the best side characters out of all the Persona games so it's worth it hanging out with those one too) and get boosts for fusions.

Fusion is a system where you fuse 2 or more Personas (which are the monsters you use to battle) to get stronger Personas. Fusions do have the issue that they're too complicated though, but that probably won't affect you unless you try to get every single Persona.

As for the dungeon crawling part of the game, it's honestly pretty fun but it's really dated which can lead to it becoming pretty annoying. A lot of weird things can happen that may feel very unfair. However it's really simple and it's not too hard. I played it on hard difficulty and didn't have much of a hard time.

Overall Persona 4 Golden is an 8/10 game that's only dragged down by dated gameplay that feels unfair sometimes. If you want a possibly better (and seemingly even easier) experience and you have the money you can wait for the upcoming remake, but I think this version is worth trying out too.

I just finished this game last night and managed to get the best ending.
And wow, I am incredibly impressed with Persona 4 Golden.

To be honest, I completed Persona 3 Reload right before this just to follow the proper lore order.
Going from that to this, the graphics and music are obviously a significant downgrade.

Not only that, but when I explored the first dungeon even on Normal difficulty, the game felt brutally hard, especially when it came to managing each character's SP.

In my personal opinion, the most challenging dungeon in the game isn't the final dungeon, but rather the first one, because you literally have no items and only default equipment.

I was seriously conflicted at one point and even tried escaping to Persona 5 Royal for a few hours, thinking about skipping this game entirely.
After all, Persona 4 Revival is on the horizon and I am highly anticipating it.

However, when it comes to the story, Persona 4 Golden easily clears Persona 3 Reload by a mile.
As for the graphics and music, they were definitely cool for their time, though obviously not by modern standards.

Furthermore, the Social Link stories in this game are far more engaging and memorable than the ones in P3R.
We also have a place that we can proudly and warmly call "home" here, rather than just a dormitory.

In the end, I am so grateful that I decided to come back to this game and was able to achieve the True/Golden Ending.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the control scheme can feel clunky and difficult to get used to when maneuvering the character through the central shopping district and dungeons.

citations.review_text:
[h2] "Doesn't matter how far apart we are. The bonds we've made will remain strong. Everyone's hearts is connected to the people they know and trust. It's those bonds that let us all search for our purpose in life. As long as it's a purpose that you believe in, there will always be someone who could help you fulfill it. You, me, and everyone else, there are no barriers. Our hearts are one. Right, Sensei?" [/h2]
[h3] - Teddie [/h3]

Persona 4 Golden is a game that is one of a kind, there isn't much masterpieces like this, it is most definitely worth all of your money, or even more.

The game's core theme is self acceptance, this game does a good job at that; each member has their own struggles that they have to overcome and accept. 
Speaking of cast, they're without a doubt pretty amazing to watch, watch them interact, accept oneself, many more. 

P4G's combat isn't the best; it's quite wanky, but the game is almost 14 years old, so that had to be expected! Even so, I had plenty of fun going throughout the dungeons; compared to P3R's Tartarus, they are definitely way more fun and not as grindy!

The true ending was a lovely conclusion! As for the social links, most of them are pretty memorable and meaningful. I'd love to talk more about them, but I don't want to spoil.
The game has a lot, and I mean A LOT of funny moments. I don't know what to say about them too much, but I guarantee fun time out of them and the game in general! 

For $20 you get an unforgettable game you won't regret spending a dollar on.
I dropped P4G for a few months because I kept failing at the beginning; however, I am glad for giving it a shot, as I said the characters are great, social links are amazing, and an interesting mystery and tons of funny moments along with the thrill of solving a murder case.

I recommend this game for anyone and everyone. 10/10

First of all, I wish Yosuke was a romance option, I really ship him with the main character. Highly recommend! The game feels so comforting to me, it feels like home. I had a blast playing it and meeting each character. Their world feels so full and exciting, never a dull moment. It made my every day better and I always look forward what's going to happen next! I couldn't stop playing and when I was close to the finale, I didn't want it to end! It has thrilling and emotional moments that are now instilled in my being. 

I enjoyed the social links very much but my absolute favorites were the: Hierophant, Death, and Hanged Man. It made me tear up, it was so beautiful. It's so worth it doing all the social links! I also feel very attached to the main characters, they are so lovable. I just didn't like those typical "fanservice" moments, it wasn't for me and I don't get why they always have to include those certain moments since some are similar to P3R haha. Not a big fan of that but okay. The controls were also clunky, I don't know if it was just me, it took a bit of time to get used to the perspective and the controls, it was kind of annoying and funny at first because it was hard to control the main character. I run on zigzags in the central shopping district lmao. I use a controller so I just used the camera for smoother movements haha. That made things easier for me in dungeons.

Overall, I still had a very good time and I ended up really loving the game so much! I can't wait for the revival and to see them all again. It's now entrenched in my psyche.

claims.claim: Reviewers recommend using community mods like the P4G Community Enhancement Pack or Reloaded II to add quality-of-life features and restore original graphics and openings.

citations.review_text: I can recommend this game to anyone who has even the slightest interest in JRPGs. The story is very good, I liked almost all the characters, the music is perfect, and the gameplay is a lot of fun — even though it lacks the quality-of-life features that were added in later installments. I’d also recommend the “P4G Community Enhancement Pack” to everyone, as it adds a few quality-of-life features as well as minor general improvements.

Greatest game of all time. 

Doubles as a great filter against people who don't actually like Persona or MegaTen as a whole too: I have yet to see one criticism of this game that isn't "it's heccin old so it's bad or whatever" from the type of guy who buys the new Madden every year, or newgens complaining about the dungeons (even though they had no problem with Tartarus in P3R apparently) and the "problematic media" that is a story of self-acceptance and triumph over delusion.
PS: Make sure to mod in the original Persona 4's opening and fog graphics for the best experience though, it really adds a lot (you can do this easily using Reloaded II).

While P4G doesn't quite have the sauce of the newer persona games, the aesthetic and music still hold up nicely, as long as you're okay with PS2-era graphics. The combat/dungeon crawling can feel tedious at times, but I feel that the surrounding systems (time management, persona fusion, team building) offer lots of interesting decisions to make up for it. The overall plot was engaging as well, even as someone who knew the killer was going into the game for the first time. Some of the events with the group, specifically the tropey ones, felt a bit miserable to get through. Overall I felt that a lot of the moments with the characters were enjoyable though. Specifically, a few of the social links (e.g. Kanji, Naoki, and the Dojimas) were fantastic side-stories. 

Definitely would recommend if you're down for turn-based combat, but also it's probably worth waiting to see how P4R turns out.

Probably my favorite out of the 3 main persona games.

Revival is definitely going to improve on the gameplay, so I can't wait for that.
